newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says steel unit needs less capital.
newsitem.headline: BHP says steel unit needs less capital.

text.p: The Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it was reducing the amount of capital employed in the steel division.

Managing director John Prescott said in response to a question at a business lunch that the company was trying to lower its debt-to-equity ratio and was cutting back on fresh capital to the steel operation in line with this aim.

"We will take on board and develop any major opportunity that comes along in any one of our businesses and we are not here to give preference to a particular group as against another group, except that we are seeking to reduce the capital employed in the steel business," Prescott said.
BHP had largely rebuilt its Australian steel facilities, which no longer need capital to be efficient.
"In short we don't need a lot of capital in the steel group," he said.
Prescott said BHP had paused development of its offshore steel units and announced it would be selling two Asian downstream steel businesses.
He said in his address that BHP may sell any non-strategic or underperforming assets, including Australian steel operations in Whyalla and Newcastle and in New Zealand.
